transcript.text: Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to get us organized around the deficiency letter response. As we all know, we have 30 calendar days to respond to the regulator, and the draft that's been circulated still leaves several key issues unresolved -- software scope, lot disposition, the pediatric indication, and which patient-data fields we'll include. We need to make concrete decisions on each of those four items before we can finalize and submit. Let's start by hearing where each of you stands and what additional information you may have that bears on those open questions.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share something important that I haven't yet incorporated into the circulated draft. After a technical call with the regulator, I received a written follow-up message confirming two specific requirements: first, that our response must be limited to software version 4.2, and second, that we must include an answer matrix with exactly six question rows. I saved that message in the regulatory mailbox but have not yet updated the draft to reflect these constraints. This directly affects the software scope question on our agenda and also constrains how we structure our overall response.

transcript.text: There's a critical commercial constraint we need to factor into our decision on the pediatric indication. I confirmed in our hospital customer's contract file that the customer has a termination right if our regulatory response withdraws or narrows the pediatric indication. This means our response to the regulator must preserve the pediatric indication as-is -- we cannot propose withdrawing or narrowing it, or we risk losing a key customer contract on top of the regulatory issue.

transcript.text: I need to share something critical on the patient-data fields question. My privacy review of the data the regulator is requesting confirmed two restrictions that must be applied: first, the submission may contain only deidentified aggregate data, and second, every reporting cell representing fewer than 10 patients must be suppressed. The circulated draft currently does not specify either of these restrictions. If we submit patient-level data or include small-cell counts, we would be exposing identifiable pediatric patient information in violation of applicable privacy requirements. These two limitations need to be explicitly written into the data-handling section of our response before it can be finalized and submitted.

commitments.detail: Update draft response to limit software scope to version 4.2 and structure the answer matrix with exactly six question rows as confirmed by the regulator's written follow-up.
Document lots L17 and L18 as on hold with calibration deviations under investigation and include corrective actions in the response before submission.
Preserve the pediatric indication as-is in the response to avoid triggering the hospital customer's contract termination right.
Revise the data-handling section to specify deidentified aggregate data only and suppress all reporting cells with fewer than 10 patients.
